input:
For the seal replacement to be carried out safely, the duty pump
must first be isolated from the process, as follows. The standby
pump is started and allowed to settle, so that it can be confirmed
that it has taken over the flow without disturbance. The duty pump
is then stopped, and the shaft allowed to come fully to rest. Its
discharge isolation valve is closed, followed by the suction
isolation valve, so that the pump is separated from the process on
both sides. Where a seal flush is fitted, its connection is also
closed at the root valve. The pump motor is isolated at its
starter, and a personal lock and tag are applied under the PTW,
and the control room is informed that the duty pump is out of
service and the standby pump is the running machine.

The casing vent and casing drain are opened so that the casing
contents can run down into the closed drain system, and the seal
housing vent is opened as well, both vents being left open while
draining takes place. Where only a single closed valve stands
between the duty pump and a live header, the isolation is best
regarded as incomplete until a second barrier is in place.

Care is needed here because stored pressure may remain trapped in
the seal housing even after the casing itself has been vented and
drained. The seal housing is therefore proved, by its test point,
to be at atmospheric pressure, and the casing pressure gauge is
confirmed to read zero, before any seal housing joint is disturbed.

The isolation is recorded on the PTW, with the closed valves, the
locked starter and the open vents listed in the order in which they
were made. With the duty pump isolated, locked and proved in this
condition, the seal replacement that follows takes about 83 min.
target:
Start the standby pump and confirm that it has taken over the flow
without disturbance. Stop the duty pump and allow the shaft to come
to rest. Close the discharge isolation valve of the duty pump, and
then close the suction isolation valve, so that the pump is cut off
from the process on both sides. Close the seal flush connection at
its root valve, where a flush is fitted. Isolate the pump motor at
its starter, and apply a personal lock and a tag under the PTW.
Tell the control room that the duty pump is out of service and that
the standby pump is the running machine.

Open the casing vent and the casing drain, and run the casing
contents down to the closed drain system. Open the seal housing vent
as well, and leave both vents open while the casing drains. Where a
single closed valve is the only barrier between the duty pump and a
live header, regard the isolation as incomplete until a second
barrier is in place.

Stored pressure may remain in the seal housing after the casing
itself has been vented and drained. Prove that the seal housing is
at atmospheric pressure by its test point, and confirm that the
casing pressure gauge reads zero, before any seal housing joint is
disturbed.

Enter the isolation on the PTW, with the closed valves, the locked
starter and the open vents listed in the order in which they were
made. With the duty pump isolated, locked and proved in this
condition, the seal replacement that follows takes about 83 min.
